finding.title: The 30 second test timeout is granted per fixture, not per test
finding.mechanism: AsyncTestHarness.TestCancellationToken creates a single CancellationTokenSource on first access and keeps it for the lifetime of the harness. NUnit constructs one fixture instance and reuses it for every [Test] in that fixture, so all of them share one budget. Once it is spent, every later test that honours the token fails at once.
finding.origin: Present in the imported upstream sources; not introduced by this slice.

twoCellExperiment.why: Same test, same build, same broker. The only variable is what ran before it in its fixture.

cellA.what: the whole Failing_to_connect_to_rabbitmq fixture in order

twoCellExperiment.reading: Alone the test passes and is allowed to run 60 s. After two predecessors spent 40 s of the shared budget it fails after 0.037 s with TaskCanceledException. The test is not slow and not flaky; it is starved.

secondDefectOppositeDirection.title: The Turnout fixture is a scenario, not five independent tests
secondDefectOppositeDirection.reading: Complete and in order the fixture is green in 1.4 s. The [Order(4)] test alone never completes, because only [Order(1)] submits the job. Cases 2..5 assert on state produced by case 1 and cannot stand alone.

disprovenHypotheses.hypothesis: The delayed message exchange plugin drops the second, longer delay.
disprovenHypotheses.measurement: Direct plugin probe over the management API, no product code: 1000 ms then 2000 ms, published sequentially, three rounds.
disprovenHypotheses.result: 6 of 6 delivered, 1.0 s and 2.0 s as scheduled.

disprovenHypotheses.hypothesis: Recreating the virtual host per fixture destroys pending delayed messages and poisons the plugin for the next test.
disprovenHypotheses.measurement: Five paired rounds: control against a clean vhost, and a vhost deleted while a 30 s delayed message was still pending.
disprovenHypotheses.result: 5 of 5 control and 5 of 5 poisoned delivered at ~1.0 s.

disprovenHypotheses.hypothesis: The per fixture virtual host reset is itself expensive enough to consume the budget and degrades over a long run.
disprovenHypotheses.measurement: 120 consecutive delete plus create cycles against the pinned image.
disprovenHypotheses.result: median 75 ms, max 102 ms, no trend (first 20 median 74 ms, last 20 median 75 ms), 9.0 s over 120 fixtures.

blastRadius.note: Fixtures in the required run whose tests together outlive the one budget they share. Every listed test ran with an already exhausted or nearly exhausted budget; that some of them still pass only means they never touched the token.
blastRadius.conservative: This count is a lower bound. The budget clock starts at the first access to the token, which for a broker fixture happens during setup, before the first test's measured duration begins. The Turnout fixture proves it: its [Order(1)] test measures 29.6 s, just under the threshold used here, yet its [Order(4)] test still failed after 0.0005 s because the budget was already gone.

notYetExplained.observation: Both are [Order(1)] or single tests, so they start with a full budget, and both took 29.6 s and 29.8 s in the required run while passing in 1.4 s and in five of five isolated runs. Their failure is therefore not the shared budget. Both use the delayed message scheduler, whose plugin is measured healthy above, so the cause is still open.
